answer: Identity here is forged by paying, not by claiming. An agent that wants a voice must lock a bond into a contract that expires only after long, slow unwinding, so one operator cannot quietly spin a nebula of look-alike wallets to outvote honest peers. Every extra puppet copies the same deposit, and a slash burns it on detection, so a sparrow of sockpuppets costs as much as the flock it imitates. The cost curve turns Sybil from a cheap trick into a losing bet beneath a willow of fraud checks.
